llm.thesis: AppLovin has de-rated violently (-52% over 12m, -57% from the 52-week high, 33% below its 200-day) while the reported fundamentals went the other way: TTM revenue +22.4% (accelerating from +13.7%), 84% operating margin, 69.6% FCF margin, ROIC 130%, net debt/EBITDA 0.08x and a 2.3% buyback yield with share count down 1.8%. That gap between reality (71) and pricing (24) is the trade — but the honest version of it is narrower than the headline P/E of 24x at the 0th percentile of its own history suggests, because the margin and EPS explosion (+3,201bps operating margin, +85% EPS on +22% revenue) is heavily mix-driven following the shift to a pure advertising model, so trailing earnings are a poor forward anchor. The cleaner anchors — 16.2x EV/Sales and 18.8x EV/EBITDA — say the stock is fairly priced, not distressed, for ~20%+ growth with best-in-class cash conversion (1.03x). The asymmetry is therefore not 'deep value', it is 'a compounder whose multiple has already reset to a defensible level while the business is still accelerating' — attractive, but requiring the next print to confirm that the growth rate, not just the margin optics, is real.
llm.fundamental_read: This is an extraordinarily high-quality cash engine: $6.50B TTM revenue, $5.46B operating income, $4.53B FCF, 1.03x FCF conversion, ROIC 130% and incremental ROIC capped at the engine's 500% ceiling — all on a near-debt-free balance sheet (net debt $462M, 0.08x EBITDA, 27.5x interest coverage). Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly: $2.45B of buybacks and a -1.8% diluted share count, with SBC a modest 4.4% of revenue. The caution is that gross margin of 89.7% and R&D of only $253M on $6.5B of revenue imply a post-divestiture, asset-light reporting mix, so the 3,201bps of YoY operating margin expansion overstates true underlying operating leverage and makes the 67.8% net margin and 24x P/E unreliable as a forward multiple. Growth acceleration (+8.7pts) is the fact that matters most; margin expansion of that magnitude cannot repeat.
llm.technical_read: The primary trend is still down: price 312.47 sits below the 20-day (318.57), 50-day (345.89) and 200-day (468.30), i.e. 33% below the long-term average, with a -29.9% three-month return. The tape is stabilizing rather than turning — RSI 43 is neutral, MACD histogram has flipped positive (+2.76) and the 1-month return is +0.6% — so this is a basing attempt, not a confirmed reversal. The operative levels are the 20/50-day cluster at ~319-346 as the first proof-of-repair; failure to reclaim them keeps the downtrend intact and a close >10% below the 200-day with negative relative strength is already the stated break condition.
llm.market_expectation: At 16.2x EV/Sales and 18.8x EV/EBITDA with a 4.3% FCF yield, the market is not pricing stagnation — it is pricing normalization: that 22% growth decelerates as the gaming ad base matures and the newer self-serve/e-commerce vertical ramps more slowly than the bull case, and that the current margin structure is a peak rather than a base. The 52% drawdown alongside a +66 Technology rotation score tells you capital is flowing into the sector but actively avoiding this name, which implies a stock-specific credibility discount (attribution/measurement scrutiny, sustainability of the AI-ranking edge, or disbelief in reported economics) that the fundamental screen cannot see. In short: the market accepts the cash flows but doubts their durability and growth rate.
what_market_misses: The multiple has already done most of the work: EV/Sales at the 27th percentile of its own 5y range while revenue growth is accelerating +8.7pts means the market is extrapolating deceleration into an accelerating number.
Shareholder yield is doing quiet compounding — $2.45B of buybacks against a $105B cap with a -1.8% share count, executed into a 57% drawdown, adds EPS growth independent of revenue.

Balance sheet optionality is underrated: 0.08x net leverage and $4.5B of annual FCF means the company can buy back aggressively, acquire, or absorb a demand air-pocket without dilution or refinancing risk.
Capital is rotating into Technology (+66, the strongest sector score by a wide margin) while this name has not participated — a mean-reversion setup if any single print restores credibility.
Conversely, what the bull screen misses: the 24x P/E at the 0th historical percentile is a mix artifact, so 'cheapest ever' is an illusion; the real multiple is 16x sales.
catalysts: Next quarterly report (~90 days after the 2026-08-05 filing) — the single most important event, as it must confirm that revenue growth held above the low-20s without the divestiture mix tailwind.
Continued aggressive buyback execution at depressed prices (current 2.3% buyback yield) as a visible capital-allocation signal.
Technical repair: reclaiming the 50-day (~346) and then the 200-day (~468) would confirm that the Technology rotation (+66) is finally reaching the name.
Evidence that the AI Software & Agents constraint — 'trust, integration into workflows, proprietary data' — is easing, i.e. third-party validation of the ad-ranking model's incrementality.
Any resolution of the unexplained stock-specific discount (short-report rebuttal, disclosure enhancement, guidance reinstatement) that the quantitative screen cannot capture.
risks: Margin normalization: 84% operating margin and 67.8% net margin are structurally implausible to sustain; a reversion toward a normalized mix would mechanically expand the P/E from 24x toward the EV/Sales-implied level.

The engine reports 'no flagged risks' while the stock is down 52% — that divergence itself is the risk signal; the market is likely pricing information (accounting scrutiny, attribution methodology, advertiser concentration) not present in this evidence set.
Revenue concentration in a mobile gaming advertiser base that is cyclically and structurally mature; the e-commerce/self-serve expansion is the growth bridge and it is unproven in this data.
Privacy/attribution regime changes at the platform level (ATT-style policy shifts) can impair targeting efficacy and thus pricing power with little warning.
ROE of 139% is flattered by a shrunken equity base ($3.16B) from buybacks — it is a leverage-of-capital-structure artifact as much as an operating fact.

Macro regime is effectively uninformative — Goldilocks 26.6% vs Contraction 25.4% and Stagflation 23.5% is near-uniform; advertising budgets are the first cut in a contraction and macro fit is only 53/100.
Technically the stock is 33% below its 200-day; drawdowns of this magnitude often continue longer than fundamental screens expect.
thesis_break_conditions: TTM revenue growth falls below 16% (currently 22.4%) — the acceleration is the core of the thesis.
Operating margin compresses more than 200bps YoY or gross margin falls materially from 89.7%, confirming the margin structure was mix-driven and transient.
FCF conversion drops below ~0.85x (currently 1.03x) or FCF growth turns negative, breaking the cash-compounding leg.
Buyback pace slows materially or diluted share count turns positive, signalling management no longer views the stock as cheap.
Price closes >10% below the 200-day with negative relative strength while Technology rotation stays positive — i.e. the sector bid exists and the stock still fails.
Technology rotation score turns below -20 for two consecutive runs, or adverse regime (Stagflation + Contraction) probability exceeds 55%.
AI Software & Agents theme trend drops below 45.
Any restatement, auditor change, or disclosure event that calls the reported 84% operating margin into question.
second_order_beneficiaries: Accelerated compute and cloud infrastructure providers: the ad-ranking/AI model that produces the 130% ROIC is inference-hungry, so training and serving capacity suppliers monetize AppLovin's core competitive input.

Independent measurement, attribution and incrementality-verification vendors: the binding constraint on this business model is advertiser trust in self-reported attribution — whoever adjudicates that captures budget-gating power.
Mobile app publishers and game studios on the supply side: an advertiser-demand engine bidding aggressively raises effective CPMs and monetization for inventory owners.
CTV and non-mobile inventory owners: as the platform expands beyond its gaming base, incremental supply sources gain pricing leverage.

E-commerce and payments infrastructure: the growth bridge runs through direct-response commerce advertisers, so checkout, merchant-data and catalog-feed infrastructure vendors sit downstream of the same spend.
Rival demand-side and retail-media networks: if advertisers diversify away from a single opaque black-box bidder, competing managed-bidding platforms absorb the reallocated budget.

epistemic_labels.statement: TTM revenue $6.504B, +22.4% YoY, accelerating from +13.7% the prior quarter.
Operating margin 84.0%, up 3,201bps YoY; net margin 67.8%; gross margin 89.7%.
FCF $4.53B, FCF margin 69.6%, FCF conversion 1.03x; ROIC 130%; net debt/EBITDA 0.08x.
$2.45B of buybacks with diluted share count down 1.8% YoY; SBC 4.4% of revenue.
Stock -52% over 12m, -57.4% from 52w high, 33.3% below the 200-day; RSI 43, MACD histogram positive.
P/E 23.8x sits at the 0th percentile of its own 5y history (median 91.7x); EV/Sales 16.2x at the 27th percentile; PEG 0.28.
Technology is the strongest rotation score at +66; all sectors ex-Energy are negative.
The 3,201bps margin expansion and the 0th-percentile P/E are substantially mix artifacts of a shift to a pure advertising reporting base, so trailing EPS overstates forward earnings power.
At 16.2x EV/Sales and 18.8x EV/EBITDA, the stock is fairly valued rather than deeply discounted; 'cheapest ever' is measured against a prior bubble multiple.
The 52% drawdown occurring alongside accelerating fundamentals implies stock-specific information (credibility, attribution methodology, or disclosure concerns) not captured in this evidence set.
The market expects growth to decelerate and margins to normalize from current peak levels.
Regime probabilities are near-uniform (Goldilocks 26.6 / Contraction 25.4 / Reflation 24.6 / Stagflation 23.5), meaning macro provides little directional edge here.
Advertiser demand for third-party incrementality verification becomes the gating factor for the next leg of budget share, creating a monetizable niche for independent measurement providers.
A single credible quarterly print holding growth above 20% ex-mix could trigger a rapid multiple re-rating given the sector bid and the 47-point expectations gap.
